why:
Quote and cited lines are accurate, but the load-bearing sentence of the claimed our-state — "The only gate is whole-workspace trust; inside a trusted project every `.mcp.json` server is materialized without an individual approve/reject step" — is false in three separate ways. This is the mcp.md twin of f029 (settings.md) and fails for the same reason, verified independently here.

1. QUOTE — VERBATIM. `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md` line 418, read whole: "For security reasons, Claude Code prompts for approval before using project-scoped servers from `.mcp.json` files. If you need to reset these approval choices, use the `claude mcp reset-project-choices` command." The second sentence reinforces rather than reverses. Related context at :169 (`⏸ Pending approval`), :173 (v2.1.196 — approvals are read only after workspace trust), :206 (`enabledMcpjsonServers`/`disabledMcpjsonServers` control `.mcp.json` approval). `mcp` is row 128 of `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`, so it is a valid Claude contract page.

2. CITED LINES — ACCURATE. `native-sources.ts:995` is exactly `if (context.projectTrustState === 'trusted') {`; `:1067` is where `.mcp.json` becomes records via `mcpServerRecords(...)`. `project-config.ts:190-215` is the body of `parseMcpServersDocument`, which validates shape and warns, and gates nothing. A NUL-safe `grep -rna` over `packages/` and `apps/` finds `enabledMcpjsonServers`, `disabledMcpjsonServers`, `enableAllProjectMcpServers` and `reset-project-choices` in NO source file (only in `docs/architecture/unified-plugin-adapter-runtime.md:198` prose and the sweep's own JSON). That identifier-absence half holds.

3. ONE LAYER UP — REFUTES THE CONSEQUENCE. `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:699-708` filters the native inventory per record before the resolver sees it:

    if (!isPiCapabilityTurn) return true
    if (record.kind === 'mcp' && !isManagedMcpServerAllowed(managedPiPolicy, {
      name: record.logicalName,
      ...record.mcpServerIdentity,
    })) return false

That is a real per-server approve/reject list — managed `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers` (`managed-policy.ts:129-130`, `isManagedMcpServerAllowed` at `:1573`) — and it matches on transport/url/command identity, not just name, with the comment citing `managed-mcp.md:150` so "a denied server cannot escape by being renamed." `mcpServerRecords` emits one record per declared server, so this runs per `.mcp.json` server inside a trusted project. Claude's own `disabledMcpjsonServers: ["filesystem"]` example is expressible today as a managed `deniedMcpServers` entry.

ONE LAYER DOWN — TRUST IS NOT BLIND. `packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts:107-128` (`detectMcpServers`) runs PRE-trust and surfaces the `.mcp.json` server SLUGS by name (keys only, never url/command/env, size-capped, non-regular-file-safe). The user therefore sees the exact list of servers a project declares before granting trust — the review half of "prompts for approval before using project-scoped servers."

WRONG SUBSYSTEM NAMED. The gate is PROJECT trust, not "whole-workspace trust": `ProjectTrustStore` (`capabilities/project-trust-store.ts`) is keyed by `ProjectKey` + `identityFingerprint`, and `SessionManager.setProjectTrust` (`:14537`) operates on a `projectHandleId`. A separate workspace-level `capabilities/trust-store.ts` exists, so naming it is the sibling-subsystem error this repo's audit history calls a refutation. A reset equivalent also exists at project granularity — `setProjectTrust(..., 'blocked')` re-decides the record and drains bound sessions — so "no reset command exists" is true only of a per-server reset.

Not in `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` §3 (all nine checked: seatbelt wildcard, availableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, three SessionMirrorStore rows — none is this). Its post-§5 addendum does record the Pi-only bound of this very filter. Not a de-brand, dropped-subscription or gateway difference.
correctedState:
A narrower row is worth re-filing; the row as written must not be acted on, because it would add gating on top of gating that already exists and would target the wrong store.

WHAT IS THERE: a project `.mcp.json` server passes two gates and one disclosure. (1) PROJECT trust — `native-sources.ts:995` (`projectTrustState === 'trusted'`), keyed per project by `ProjectTrustStore` (ProjectKey + identity fingerprint), revocable via `SessionManager.setProjectTrust(..., 'blocked')` at `:14537`. (2) A per-server managed allow/deny filter over each individual server record — `storage-runtime.ts:699-708` calling `isManagedMcpServerAllowed(managedPiPolicy, { name, ...mcpServerIdentity })`, i.e. Claude's `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers` from `managed-mcp.md`, enforced on url/command identity so a rename cannot evade it. (3) Pre-trust disclosure of the declared server slugs by name — `project-contribution-detect.ts:107-128`.

WHAT IS GENUINELY MISSING, with its bounds: the USER-tier half of the approval, plus the pending/rejected status vocabulary. Claude's `enabledMcpjsonServers`/`disabledMcpjsonServers`/`enableAllProjectMcpServers` are settable at user/project/local scope; our equivalent exists only at the MANAGED policy tier, so a user with no fleet policy faces all-or-nothing project trust and cannot reject one server of a `.mcp.json` while accepting the rest. There is likewise no post-trust per-server off switch: a native `.mcp.json` row renders no toggle (`McpServersPanel.tsx:356` — `onToggle` requires `row.originKind === 'plugin'`), and `resolver.ts:1601-1613` plus `storage-runtime.ts:849-858` deliberately EXEMPT `kind === 'mcp'` from session selection under a decided R3 contract, so any fix must change that contract explicitly rather than by side effect. Second bound: the managed filter is skipped entirely off Pi — `storage-runtime.ts:632` `isPiCapabilityTurn = context.provider === 'pi'` and `:699` `if (!isPiCapabilityTurn) return true` — already recorded in the `2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md` addendum. There is no `⏸ Pending approval` / `✘ Rejected` reporting state anywhere.
